<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par119 />the verb (intransitive) construed with {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} has a greater independence, and consequently more emphasis than the verb construed with a direct accusative; the latter conveys a sort of necessary specification of the action, while the noun introduced by {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} is used rather as a merely adverbial complement. An instructive example of this is {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן קוֹל|translate=vocem emittere}}, ''to utter a voice'', also ''to thunder'', while in {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן בְּקוֹלוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=7}} (68:34, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=8}}), {{GHGheb|text=נָתַן}} has an independent sense = ''he thundered with his voice'' (i.e. mightily).

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|r}}
(''c'') {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}<ref>Cf. Giesebrecht, ''Die hebr. Präpos. Lamed'', Halle, 1876.</ref> ''to'', a very general expression of ''direction towards'' anything, is used to represent the most varied ''relations'' of an action or state with regard to a person or thing. On the use of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} as a periphrasis for the ''genetivus poseessoris'' or ''auctoris'' (the idea of belonging to), see § 129; on {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with the passive, to introduce the author or the cause, see {{GHGpar|121|f}}; on {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} in a purely local sense (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לִימִֽינְךָ|translate=at thy right hand}}, prop. ''towards thy right hand''), or temporal (e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לָעֶ֫רֶב|translate=at evening}}, &c.) or distributive, see the Lexicon

The following uses of {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} properly belong to the government of the verb:

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|s}}
(1) As a ''nota dativi''<ref>Just as in the Romance languages the Latin preposition ''ad'' (Italian ''a'', before vowels ''ad>'', French ''à'', Spanish ''á'') and in English ''to'' are used as a periphrasis for the dative.—On the introduction of the nearer object by {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, cf. {{GHGpar|117|n}}.</ref> to introduce the remoter object; also

(2) To introduce the ''dativus commodi''. This ''dativus commodi'' (or ''incommodi'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=11}}) is used—especially in colloquial language and in later style—in the form of a pronoun with {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, as an apparently pleonastic ''dativus ethicus'', with many verbs, in order to give emphasis to the significance of the occurrence in question ''for'' a particular subject. In this construction the person of the pronoun must always agree with that of the verbal form.<ref>Such expressions as the analogous English ''he plucked me ope his doublet, but me no buts'', and the like, are accordingly inadmissible in Hebrew.</ref> By far the most frequent use of this {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} is with the pronoun of the 2nd person after imperatives, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לֶךְ־לְךָ|translate=go, got thee away}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=2|verse=13}} (also in the feminine, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=10}}, 13); {{GHGheb|text=נְטֵה לְךָ|translate=turn thee aside}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=סְעוּ לָכֶם|translate=take your journey}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=עִבְדוּ לָכֶם|translate=pass ye over}}; {{GHGheb|text=בְּדַח־לְךָ|translate=flee}} (to save thyself), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=43}}; {{GHGheb|text=עֲלִי־לָךְ|translate=get thee up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=40|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=פְּנוּ לָכֶם|translate=turn you}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=40}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּבוּ לָכֶם|translate=return ye}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=27}}; {{GHGheb|text=ק֫וּמִי לָךְ|translate=rise up}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=שְׁבוּ לָכֶם|translate=abide ye}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=חֲדַל לְךָ|translate=forbear thee}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=21}} (in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=22}}); {{GHGheb|text=הָ֫בוּ לָכֶם|translate=take you}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=18|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=20}}, and so almost regularly {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּׁ֫מֶד לְךָ}} (see above, {{GHGpar|51|n}}) ''cave tibi!'' and {{GHGheb|text=הִשָּֽׁמְלוּ לָכֶם|translate=take heed to yourselves}}; {{GHGheb|text=דְמֵה רְךָ|translate=be thou like}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=2|verse=17}} (cf. verse 9), 8:14, is remarkable; after a perfect consecutive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=17|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=22|verse=5}}; after an imperfect consecutive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=36|verse=9}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּבְטַח לְךָ|translate=and puttest thy trust}}.—In the 3rd person, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּ֫שֶׁב לָהּ|translate=and sat her down}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=16}}, cf. 22:5, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=27}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=120|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=123|verse=4|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=19}}; even after a participle, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=8|verse=9}}.—In the 1st person plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=37|verse=11}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|t}}
(3) To introduce the result after verbs of making, forming, changing, appointing ''to'' something, esteeming ''as'' something; in short, in all those cases in which, according to {{GHGpar|117|ii}}, a second ''accusative'' may also be used.

{{GHGmargin-letter|119|u}}
(4) In loose connexion with some verbal idea in the sense of ''in reference to, with regard to''... ({{GHGpar|143|e}}); so after a {{GHGterm|verbum dicendi}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=20|verse=13}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=23}}, cf.<section end=par119 /><noinclude>
